drhp.business: Manufactures and trades carded, combed and compact combed cotton yarns (counts Ne 26 to Ne 40) and cotton bales at a semi-automated integrated spinning-and-ginning facility in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat. Cotton bales are used both for captive yarn production and for sale to other spinning units; yarns serve knitting/weaving end-uses (denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, home and industrial textiles). Operates exclusively B2B, selling directly within Gujarat and, for out-of-state/export markets, through a reseller arrangement with 7 Seas Impex.
drhp.end_markets: Textile manufacturers, yarn exporters, bulk purchasers, fabric processors (B2B)|Denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, bottom wear, home textiles, industrial fabrics|Cotton seed to oil-extraction/animal-feed industries; cotton waste to non-woven/open-end yarn makers|Predominantly domestic (Gujarat direct; rest of India / exports via reseller 7 Seas Impex)
drhp.expansion: The principal growth step is the acquisition of Falcon Yarns Private Limited (a spinning company) funded from the Issue proceeds (Rs 11,151 lakhs part payment plus Rs 1,000 lakhs inter-corporate deposit for Falcon's working capital), which adds spinning capacity and scale to the existing 25,920-spindle / 7,700 MT yarn and 12,000 MT cotton-bale integrated facility at Halvad. The company has also built captive renewable power (solar + wind) to reduce operating costs.
drhp.mdna: Cotton bale (raw material) price exposure managed via order-linked hedging procurement and seasonal buffer stock|Seasonal ginning unit (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March) driving inventory build-up|Customer concentration (top-10 customers 59.94% in FY2025) and supplier concentration (top-10 73.05% in FY2025)|Captive renewable power reducing electricity cost|Product mix between cotton yarn, cotton bales and by-products
drhp.oem: 7 Seas Impex (reseller for out-of-Gujarat and export sales)
drhp.one_liner: Aastha Spintex Limited is a Gujarat-based B2B manufacturer of carded, combed and compact combed 100% cotton yarns and cotton bales, operating an integrated spinning-and-ginning facility at Halvad, Morbi.

business_ops.seasonality: Ginning unit operates seasonally (~6-7 months, mid-September/October to March, tied to the cotton harvest). Buffer cotton-bale stock is built during the peak harvest season (Oct-March) when availability is higher and prices lower, then drawn down in the off-season, driving inventory and working-capital seasonality.

supplier_concentration.note: Top-10 suppliers were 73.05% (FY25), 79.62% (FY24), 44.30% (FY23) of total purchases; >125 suppliers over 3 years, 6 of top-10 associated >5 years

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integrated: an in-house ginning unit converts raw cotton into cotton bales (the principal raw material for spinning), providing raw-material security and by-product revenue (cotton seed, cotton waste). Ginning operates seasonally (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March); shortfalls are met by sourcing bales from ginning mills/traders across Gujarat. Procurement is hedging-based (bales locked at order confirmation) with buffer stock built during the harvest season. Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop solar, 4 MW ground solar, 2.7 MW wind) reduces power cost.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Over the past five years (Fiscalv2021-Fiscal 2026), India has maintained a strong growth trajectory with a Compound Annual Growth Rate (“CAGR”) of approximately 9%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Projections indicate that by Fiscal 2031, India’s GDP will reach ₹563 trillion (US$6.6 trillion), expanding at an estimated CAGR of approximately 10% from Fiscal 2025 onward.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: For instance, China saw its private consumption grow at approximately 20% CAGR over the five years following its crossing in CY2006.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: India crossed this milestone in Fiscal 2022 and has since grown at approximately 6% CAGR.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Private Final Consumption Expenditure (“PFCE”), the largest GDP component, has grown at approximately 11% CAGR over Fiscal 2020–25, from ₹122.4 trillion (US$1.4 trillion) to ₹203.0 trillion (US$2.4 trillion), with discretionary spending rising to approximately 48% of total consumption (vs. 40-43% a decade ago), reflecting a clear shift toward lifestyle and experiential categories.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: As per Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), India’s Gross National Income per capita reached ₹0.23 million (US$2,666) in Fiscal 2025, growing at a approximately 8.6% CAGR since Fiscal 2020 as one of the fastest rates among comparable economies.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Smartphones are now the primary mode of internet access, with users expected to grow from 692-706 million in Fiscal 2025 to 960-1,080 million by Fiscal 2030, a 7-9% CAGR increase.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Consumers are increasingly drawn to digital-first experiences across payments, commerce, mobility, and utilities, creating multiple entry points into the formal financial ecosystem. 1.4 Rising income and digitization are enabling rapid financial inclusion but there remains headroom for growth Gross savings of the household sector in India have grown at a constant CAGR of approximately 9% from Fiscal 2020-24 and is estimated to be approximately ₹54.6 trillion according to the second advance estimates of annual gross domestic product by MoSPI.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Within financial assets, insurance has grown at a healthy CAGR of approximately 12% between Fiscal 2020 and Fiscal 2024.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Greater comfort with digital finance: UPI transaction value grew at approximately 65% CAGR from ₹21 trillion in Fiscal 2020 to ₹257 trillion in Fiscal 2025, with 80% of this growth coming from Tier-2+ cities, reflecting growing trust in digital systems and increasing convenience-led adoption. 3.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Expanding participation in financial markets: Demat penetration reached 11-13% of adults, NSE retail investor count touched 40 million, and retail loan disbursements hit approximately ₹78 trillion in Fiscal 2025 (approximately 25% CAGR from Fiscal 2020), indicating broader engagement across equity, credit, and investment products. 4.

overview.business_model: Earns revenue from manufacturing and trading carded/combed/compact combed cotton yarns and cotton bales, plus by-products (cotton seed, cotton waste). Cotton bales are used captively for yarn and sold externally; yarn is sold B2B directly within Gujarat and, for other states/exports, via a reseller (7 Seas Impex). Procurement is hedging-based (cotton bales locked at order confirmation) with seasonal buffer stock during the Oct-March harvest.

summary.oneLiner: Aastha Spintex Limited is a Gujarat-based B2B manufacturer of carded, combed and compact combed 100% cotton yarns and cotton bales, operating an integrated spinning-and-ginning facility at Halvad, Morbi.
summary.business: Manufactures and trades carded, combed and compact combed cotton yarns (counts Ne 26 to Ne 40) and cotton bales at a semi-automated integrated spinning-and-ginning facility in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat. Cotton bales are used both for captive yarn production and for sale to other spinning units; yarns serve knitting/weaving end-uses (denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, home and industrial textiles). Operates exclusively B2B, selling directly within Gujarat and, for out-of-state/export markets, through a reseller arrangement with 7 Seas Impex.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integrated: an in-house ginning unit converts raw cotton into cotton bales (the principal raw material for spinning), providing raw-material security and by-product revenue (cotton seed, cotton waste). Ginning operates seasonally (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March); shortfalls are met by sourcing bales from ginning mills/traders across Gujarat. Procurement is hedging-based (bales locked at order confirmation) with buffer stock built during the harvest season. Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop solar, 4 MW ground solar, 2.7 MW wind) reduces power cost.

customers.body: 7 Seas Impex (reseller for out-of-Gujarat and export sales)

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Cotton bale (raw material) price exposure managed via order-linked hedging procurement and seasonal buffer stock
- Seasonal ginning unit (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March) driving inventory build-up
- Customer concentration (top-10 customers 59.94% in FY2025) and supplier concentration (top-10 73.05% in FY2025)
- Captive renewable power reducing electricity cost
- Product mix between cotton yarn, cotton bales and by-products

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The principal growth step is the acquisition of Falcon Yarns Private Limited (a spinning company) funded from the Issue proceeds (Rs 11,151 lakhs part payment plus Rs 1,000 lakhs inter-corporate deposit for Falcon's working capital), which adds spinning capacity and scale to the existing 25,920-spindle / 7,700 MT yarn and 12,000 MT cotton-bale integrated facility at Halvad. The company has also built captive renewable power (solar + wind) to reduce operating costs.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Integrated spinning-and-ginning operations providing raw-material (cotton bale) security and by-product revenue
- Highest ROCE and RONW amongst selected peers in Fiscal 2025 (per DRHP)
- Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop + 4 MW ground solar + 2.7 MW wind) reducing power cost
- Location advantage in Halvad, Morbi near high-quality Gujarat cotton-growing area
- Hedging-based procurement approach locking cotton bale prices at order confirmation
- Long-standing customer/supplier relationships (>250 customers over 3 years; 14 associated >5 years)

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Acquisition at Rs 33.33/share vs Falcon's Sept-2024 buyback at Rs 14.46/share; ~Rs 11,151 lakhs of Issue proceeds deployed; integration and valuation risk
- Top-10 customers were 59.94% (FY25), 84.71% (FY24), 80.88% (FY23) of product sales
- Top-10 suppliers were 73.05% (FY25), 79.62% (FY24), 44.30% (FY23) of purchases
- Cotton bale is the principal raw material; price swings and seasonal availability affect margins despite hedging
- Reliance on 7 Seas Impex for markets outside Gujarat
- All operations at one facility in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat
- Buffer cotton-bale stock during harvest season raises inventory and working-capital needs

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Acquire Falcon Yarns Private Limited using Rs 11,151 lakhs of Issue proceeds toward part payment of the Rs 13,151 lakhs consideration**
- **Provide Rs 1,000 lakhs inter-corporate deposit to fund Falcon Yarns' working capital**
- **Operate 25,920-spindle / 7,700 MT p.a. cotton yarn and 12,000 MT p.a. cotton bale integrated capacity**
- **Continue captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop solar, 4 MW ground solar, 2.7 MW wind) to reduce power cost**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Acquire Falcon Yarns Private Limited to expand spinning capacity and scale
- Continue captive-renewable-power expansion to lower power costs
- Deepen B2B customer relationships and repeat-customer base
- Leverage reseller model (7 Seas Impex) for out-of-state and export reach
